title: Monk's disastrous rehearsal and the end of Dixieland
summary: Thelonious Monk comes to the rehearsal and it goes badly, so Kenny Kersey is hired; Ben drops the Dixieland charts after two sets and the band just plays jazz.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: However, I have to say first, as we went to the rehearsal, he hadn't hired Kenny yet, and we rehearsed first without Kenny and somebody suggested that Monk --Thelonius Monk -- was at Minton's and he was out for awhile and he could use a job.

I had heard Monk play on the street, but I didn't say anything to Ben because I didn't know whether he'd fit in this combination. However, Monk came into the rehearsal and sat at the chair and we started to run down the arrangements, and Monk listened. And so Ben would stop the band and say to play some chords, and Monk thought it over, and he'd lean on one elbow and poke a couple of notes. It was a disaster rehearsal. And Ben was pretty upset.

So, after the rehearsal, Eddie Barefield suggested that we try Kenny Kersey, which worked out beautiful. So we opened at the club, and Ben opened with a couple of traditional arrangements. He kind of weakened on the second set, and demanded only an arrangement of 'Muskrat Ramble', and by the third set, he collected the arrangements and carefully put them under the piano and we never saw them again. It was the night they collected Dixieland, and we were all delighted to just play jazz. We used to have an expression, 'natural born jazz' with Ben feeding some of his Duke backgrounds behind the superb Buck Clayton and Eddie Barefield on clarinet, he was just a wonderful musician.
